headline: Hasnat Abdullah: I'll resign if corruption is proven
summary: The National Citizen Party MP challenged colleagues in parliament, responding to allegations that some former activists have betrayed the 'July spirit'.
details: National Citizen Party (NCP) MP Hasnat Abdullah declared in parliament today that he would resign from his seat if any investigation proves his involvement in corruption.
The statement came as a response to BNP MP Akhtaruzzaman, who claimed that some individuals have betrayed the ideals of the July Uprising.
Akhtaruzzaman alleged that some who once rode rickshaws now travel in luxury Prado vehicles after 'selling the spirit of July'.
Hasnat Abdullah argued that these were unsubstantiated allegations and urged the MP not to make such claims without proof.
He challenged the investigation, stating he would step down if proven involved in even one taka of corruption or any wrongdoing.
Additionally, Hasnat clarified his interactions with BNP MP Sayeed Al Noman, stating he had sought budget allocation for his constituency rather than personal money.
During the budget discussion, Hasnat also expressed concern that opposition MPs fear budget cuts in their constituencies if they criticize the government.
caption:
One taka of corruption and I'll resign.

Hasnat Abdullah issues a bold challenge in parliament.

National Citizen Party (NCP) MP Hasnat Abdullah declared in parliament today that he would resign from his seat if any investigation proves his involvement in corruption.

The statement came as a response to BNP MP Akhtaruzzaman, who claimed that some individuals have betrayed the ideals of the July Uprising.

Akhtaruzzaman alleged that some who once rode rickshaws now travel in luxury Prado vehicles after 'selling the spirit of July'.

Hasnat Abdullah argued that these were unsubstantiated allegations and urged the MP not to make such claims without proof.

He challenged the investigation, stating he would step down if proven involved in even one taka of corruption or any wrongdoing.

Additionally, Hasnat clarified his interactions with BNP MP Sayeed Al Noman, stating he had sought budget allocation for his constituency rather than personal money.

During the budget discussion, Hasnat also expressed concern that opposition MPs fear budget cuts in their constituencies if they criticize the government.

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune

headline_marked: Bangla QR payments [[mandatory from July 1]] at all merchant points
headline: Bangla QR payments mandatory from July 1 at all merchant points
summary: Bangladesh Bank launches a nationwide campaign to push digital payments, aiming to formalize the economy and improve the tax-to-GDP ratio.
details: Bangladesh Bank has announced that the interoperable Bangla QR payment system will become mandatory at all merchant payment points starting July 1.
To promote the initiative, the central bank organized a daylong campaign at its headquarters where officials made purchases from various companies using Bangla QR codes instead of cash.
Deputy Governor Md Habibur Rahman stated that the system will make payments safer and easier by allowing customers to pay exact amounts without needing physical cash.
The central bank believes wider adoption of digital payments will help formalize economic activities, expand the GDP, and bring more people into the formal financial system.
Deputy Governor Md Kabir Ahmed added that increased digital transactions would enhance transparency and expand the tax net, thereby improving the country's tax-to-GDP ratio.
Looking ahead, Bangladesh Bank plans to launch an interoperable Instant Payment System next year to enable real-time fund transfers between mobile wallets and bank accounts.
MFS provider Nagad has already integrated with Bangla QR and the National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB) network, joining a merchant network of nearly 10 lakh.
The move is expected to boost productivity, lower transaction costs, and help curb money laundering through better transaction traceability.
